attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No proof-analysis theorem currently forces a semantic EF+SAT_U certificate either to functionalize over all label tables or to localize its nonfunctionality to fewer than N^{epsilon-o(1)} source rows. EF may use global SAT structure shared by many rows through the same formula labels.
steps: Fix a batched generator G_N with M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, L_N=(log N)^d, and circuit size N^{rho+o(1)}; define H_N^SAT by XOR aggregation.
Assume SAT has circuits of size n^c. Substitute the length-L_N SAT circuit into every generated query and obtain C(H_N^SAT)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} because L_N^c=N^{o(1)}.
If max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, any i.o. lower bound C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon} contradicts SAT in P/poly; this is a valid route-level bridge, not a proof of the source lower bound.
Let D_N agree with H_N^SAT outside R_N. Hardwire equality tests for all rows in R_N where D_N is wrong, XOR the correction, and get C(H_N^SAT)<=C(D_N)+O(|R_N|N).

Instantiate Psys as EF+SAT_U. If its accepted certificates are functional over arbitrary label tables and dense at 2^{-O(L_N)}, the certificate property naturalizes. If soundness is only for the real SAT label table, the route escapes that barrier but must prove row-residual robustness.
Tried to derive a sparse D_N,R_N from an arbitrary nonfunctional EF+SAT_U proof by collecting rows whose SAT-semantic axioms are used essentially.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The transfer and row-patching lemmas are valid route-level results. They do not prove C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon}, do not prove P != NP, and do not yet yield a no-go theorem for all SAT-semantic proof systems.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: beta-zero XOR row-residual audit

assumptions: The batched generator outputs or streams all M_N queries with total circuit size N^{rho+o(1)}, not M_N independent copies of cost N^rho.
For every fixed c, SAT in P/poly supplies length-L_N circuits of size L_N^c for all sufficiently large valid N.
The source lower bound C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon} is claimed on infinitely many valid N in the same nonuniform model.
Equality to one hardwired N-bit row costs O(N) gates, so E exceptional rows cost O(EN) gates to patch.
definitions: source object: H_N^SAT:{0,1}^N->{0,1} is the XOR over M_N generated SAT instances G_N(x,j) of length L_N.
target object: nonuniform SAT circuits at input length n; the target consequence is SAT notin P/poly, hence NP not subset P/poly.
controlled interface: beta-zero compact substitution with L_N=(log N)^d=N^{o(1)}, M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, and batched generator size N^{rho+o(1)}.
target-preserving condition: q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, no nonuniform advice is hidden in G_N, and source and target use the same Boolean circuit model.
row residual: R_N subset {0,1}^N is a hardwired set of exceptional source rows where an approximator D_N may disagree with H_N^SAT.
circuit measure: C(F) denotes nonuniform fan-in two Boolean circuit size for the length-N truth table family.

equations.label: carrier_definition
equations.latex: H_N^{SAT}(x)=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)),\quad M_N\le N^{q+o(1)},\quad L_N=(\log N)^d.
equations.valid_when: Valid when each G_N(x,j) is a well-formed length-L_N SAT instance and XOR is implemented by ordinary Boolean circuits.

equations.label: beta_zero_substitution
equations.valid_when: Applies after assuming a length-n SAT circuit of size n^c and substituting it uniformly into every generated query slot.

equations.label: target_preserving_implication
equations.valid_when: Applies when the source lower bound occurs on infinitely many valid source lengths and the substitution upper bound would hold on every such length.

equations.label: row_patching_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when R_N is explicitly hardwired and equality to an N-bit source row costs O(N) gates in the same circuit model.

equations.label: residual_falsifier_threshold
equations.valid_when: Requires C(D_N) and |R_N|N to be measured at the same source length and against the same exponent threshold.

assumptions: U_N is uniformly enumerable in 2^{O(L_N)} time from N and the generator description.
A certificate verifier V_N(y,pi) is functional if soundness holds for every Boolean label vector y on U_N, not only for y=SAT|_{U_N}.
Dense means label-density at least 2^{-O(L_N)} among candidate label tables, matching the classical natural-property cutoff after restriction.
Semantic-only certificates may use real SAT structure, but then no natural-proofs obstruction is claimed without an additional functional extension.
definitions: source object: the same beta-zero XOR carrier H_N^SAT, viewed as the F_2 linear functional of the SAT label table on U_N.
target object: lower-bound certificates intended to imply C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon} and then SAT notin P/poly via L74.1.
controlled interface: Psys=EF+SAT_U, an Extended Frege checker allowed SAT truth axioms only for formulas in U_N={G_N(x,j)}.
target-preserving condition: certificates are advice-free, searchable in 2^{O(L_N)}, and their soundness is either functional over all label tables or explicitly SAT-semantic and nonrelativizing.

equations.label: functional_certificate_property
equations.valid_when: Valid when the verifier depends on the generated SAT instances only through an explicit label table y and a bounded certificate pi.

equations.label: naturalization_cutoff
equations.latex: \Pr_y[y\in\mathcal P_N]\ge 2^{-O(L_N)}\ \wedge\ V_N\in TIME(2^{O(L_N)})\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal P_N\ \text{is a constructive large label property}.
equations.valid_when: Applies only under functional soundness over arbitrary label vectors and uniform enumeration of the generated formula universe U_N.

equations.valid_when: Valid as a necessary audit condition because otherwise L74.1 patches the residual rows into a subthreshold exact circuit.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No named beta-zero XOR certificate system is known to provide DirectClusterSound(C,s) with |U_C|+w_C=O(log N) while also avoiding naturalization or sparse residual leakage.
steps: Fix Psys as a row-local existential certificate model for LB(y,s), where rows query target bits and proof bits.
For a cluster C, define Acc_C(y) by existential satisfaction of the row predicates and define P_C={y:Acc_C(y)=1}.
Completeness for T_N gives one accepting proof-view assignment; every y agreeing with T_N on U_C is accepted, so density is at least 2^{-|U_C|}.
If the proof-view CSP has projection-decision width w_C=O(log N), dynamic programming decides P_C in poly(N) time.
If DirectClusterSound(C,s) holds, P_C rejects every SIZE_m(s) truth table, hence is useful against the exact target class.
Thus any log-projection direct cluster becomes a valid large constructive useful property and faces PRF/natural-proofs pressure.
Attempting to replace DirectClusterSound by ordinary soundness fails: odd-charge Tseitin has global unsatisfiability but every proper cluster is satisfiable, so Acc_C(y)=1 for all y.
For beta-zero XOR, any certificate that leaves only a sparse residual R_N can be patched, giving C(H_N^SAT)<=S_D+O(|R_N|N) and falsifying a subthreshold source lower bound.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-level audit theorem and falsifier packet, not a proof of P != NP. Promotion still needs a named Psys instantiation, a prior-art boundary check, and a live inference-quality review.

assumptions: Cluster C_N is computable from 1^N in poly(N) time and its row set is not chosen using the candidate circuit D.
Completeness holds: Acc_{C_N}(T_N)=1 via a proof assignment compatible on all queried proof bits in C_N.
DirectClusterSound(C_N,s) holds in the same nonuniform target model SIZE_m(s), not merely as ordinary global soundness of Psys.
The existential proof-bit CSP induced by C_N has an explicit decomposition deciding Acc_C(y) in poly(N)2^{O(w_C)} time.
definitions: source object: A beta-zero XOR carrier H_N^SAT with truth table T_N in {0,1}^N, together with a row-local certificate model Psys whose verifier row r reads target bits Q_r subseteq [N], proof bits P_r, and accepts predicate A_r(y_{Q_r},pi_{P_r}).
target object: The target class is SIZE_m(s) on m=log N input bits, usually s=m^k or the exponent window required by the beta-zero XOR transfer, represented by truth tables TT(D) in {0,1}^N.

controlled interface: A cluster C of verifier rows has target projection U_C=union_{r in C} Q_r and projection-decision width w_C; Acc_C(y)=1 iff some proof assignment satisfies all A_r on y_{U_C}; DirectClusterSound(C,s) means Acc_C(TT(D))=0 for every D in SIZE_m(s).

target-preserving condition: The same explicit cluster C must be accepted by T_N, reject exactly the named SIZE_m(s) target without advice-dependent row selection, and be decidable from y with |U_C|+w_C=O(log N).
carrier observable: P_C={y in {0,1}^N: Acc_C(y)=1}; this is a route-level natural-property audit, not a P != NP claim.

assumptions: G is connected, so the only linear dependency among all vertex-incidence equations over F_2 is the xor of all vertex rows.
Ordinary soundness means the full row set V is unsatisfiable, but the route tries to use a small cluster C as a certificate.
The cluster C is proper; in particular every logarithmic cluster is proper for |V| superlogarithmic in N.

Validity/model regime: this lemma is interpreted only within the stated P vs NP branch model, with the same source object, target object, circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity assumptions used by the branch output.
definitions: source object: A connected graph G=(V,E) with charge b in {0,1}^V satisfying xor_{v in V} b_v=1; proof variables z_e sit on edges and row v asserts xor_{e incident v} z_e=b_v.
target object: The tested target truth table y is absent or queried only through dummy coordinates, so the target class SIZE_m(s) cannot affect local satisfiability.
controlled interface: A cluster C subsetneq V is accepted if there exists an assignment to edge proof variables satisfying every row in C.
target-preserving condition: The embedding into Psys must preserve row arity, proof-variable incidences, and zero or logarithmic target projection, with no hidden global parity check inside C.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: We have not proved that every named DirectClusterSound or Psys certificate necessarily has low alpha_ad; the result is a theorem-shaped falsifier for implementations that expose rankable summaries, not a universal impossibility theorem.
steps: Instantiate DirectClusterSound(C,k) as a certificate pi that induces a SAT-label row T_{m,pi} and proves local cluster consistency for the beta-zero XOR query matrix.
Abstract its openings into an adaptive cover: top transcript budget 2^{tau m}, level-l summary family size 2^{a_l m}, summary length 2^{mu_l m}, and opener circuit size 2^{omega_l m}.
For a fixed accepted pi, build a nonuniform circuit for T_{m,pi} by hardwiring all transcript tables and summaries and wiring the opener circuits; size is at most 2^{alpha_ad m+o(m)}.
Compare this upper bound with the claimed MCSP/MKtP no-side threshold 2^{theta m}; alpha_ad<theta contradicts accepted-row hardness.

Feed the same audit into the beta-zero XOR packet: functional label certificates with low adaptive cover either yield subthreshold row circuits or a sparse residual approximant, so they cannot support a valid source lower bound.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This certifies failure of a route-specific carrier class. It does not prove P != NP and does not construct the required high-adaptive-cover, advice-free hard-row source.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Cycle 74: DirectClusterSound adaptive-cover falsifier for MCSP/MKtP carriers

assumptions: Circuit model is unrestricted fan-in two Boolean circuits with nonuniform hardwiring allowed for a fixed accepted row.
The adaptive cover opens every queried truth-table bit of T_{m,pi}, not merely sampled verifier locations.
The verifier may be non-natural or proof-mediated, but its accepted row must be an actual MCSP no-side witness at threshold 2^{theta m}.
The cover parameters are uniform enough to be named, but the upper-bound circuit may hardwire the summaries; hence advice-freeness does not save a subthreshold cover.
The comparison alpha_ad<theta is interpreted with an o(1) slack margin, e.g. alpha_ad<=theta-eta for some eta>0.
definitions: source object: generated MCSP/MKtP no-side certificate family V_m(pi)->T_{m,pi} for truth tables on m input bits, claiming C(T_{m,pi})>2^{theta m}.
target object: advice-free E-uniform hard-row carrier yielding an E language with circuit lower bound 2^{delta n} after kappa-gap and distinct-image loss D.
controlled interface: adaptive proof-opening cover with top transcript exponent tau, level counts a_l, summary exponents mu_l, and opener exponents omega_l.
target-preserving condition: the selected hard row and its certificate are generated or searchable without advice within 2^{O(m)} time and preserve theta, kappa, and D under multiplexing.
DirectClusterSound(C,k) is modeled as a local cluster certificate whose row bits are opened through summaries, consistency transcripts, and semantic label openers.
C(T) denotes unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuit size of the truth-table row T, the same size notion used by MCSP no-side soundness.

equations.label: adaptive_cover_exponent
equations.valid_when: Valid when the certificate opening protocol is decomposed into transcript, summary-volume, and opener-circuit exponent ledgers.

equations.label: row_upper_bound_from_cover
equations.valid_when: Valid when the adaptive cover opens all row bits and unrestricted circuits may hardwire row-specific summaries.

equations.label: no_side_contradiction
equations.valid_when: Valid when MCSP no-side soundness requires every accepted row to exceed the same unrestricted circuit threshold.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find an accepted certificate with alpha_ad<theta; then the carrier is invalid, not merely unproved.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Finite route-specific falsifier for MCSP/MKtP certificate carriers, especially DirectClusterSound, Merkle, checkpoint, and rankable cluster implementations.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Adaptive-cover no-side falsifier: any generated MCSP/MKtP certificate carrier whose accepted row has adaptive cover exponent alpha_ad<theta cannot be a valid no-side source for threshold 2^{theta m}; the cover itself gives an unrestricted circuit for the row.

assumptions: SAT lower-bound target is the same semantic SAT predicate queried by G_N, not an auxiliary promise or advice language.
The generator G_N has circuit or uniform evaluation overhead N^{rho+o(1)} on inputs x and j.
The XOR has fan-in M_N and the cost of XOR aggregation is absorbed into N^{q+o(1)}.
The claimed source lower bound is C(H_N^SAT)>N^a for a fixed exponent a with slack over o(1) losses.
definitions: source object: beta-zero XOR SAT-query family H_N^SAT with polylogarithmic SAT query length L_N and polynomially many queries M_N.
target object: lower bound against SAT circuits of size n^c or a derived NP lower-bound consequence obtained by substitution into the XOR carrier.
controlled interface: black-box substitution of size-L_N SAT circuits into every query generated by G_N, plus the generator circuit for G_N.
target-preserving condition: the substitution preserves uniformity of G_N, uses no advice-selected hard query language, and keeps L_N^c=N^{o(1)} for every fixed c.

equations.label: beta_zero_parameters
equations.valid_when: Valid when beta equals zero and all SAT queries have polylogarithmic length in the carrier input scale.

equations.label: substitution_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when SAT has circuits of size n^c and G_N is implementable with the stated overhead.

equations.label: magnification_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the lower bound and substitution upper bound are compared in the same circuit model and length scale.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a<=max{rho,q}, the claimed barely-nontrivial source lower bound is below the substitution cap and has no valid target transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative transfer audit for the beta-zero XOR packet; prevents repeating a hardness-magnification slogan without the exact exponent gate.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Beta-zero XOR substitution cap: for H_N^SAT(x)=xor_{j<=M_N}SAT(G_N(x,j)) with M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, L_N=(log N)^d, and generator overhead N^{rho+o(1)}, any target consequence from a lower bound C(H_N^SAT)>N^a must have a>max{rho,q}; otherwise the beta-zero construction supplies no separation-strength transfer.

assumptions: The row model charges O(N) gates to hardwire and test one exceptional N-bit row slice.
D_N agrees with H_N^SAT on all nonresidual rows, not merely with high probability.
The lower-bound threshold is compared against the full corrected circuit D_N plus residual patches.
The residual set is uniform or explicitly encoded; hidden advice for R_N is not allowed in a positive transfer claim.
definitions: source object: beta-zero XOR truth-table or row matrix H_N^SAT with a certificate-derived approximant D_N.
target object: claimed circuit lower bound C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon} in the same nonuniform circuit model.
controlled interface: residual correction by hardwiring all exceptional rows and XORing them with D_N.
target-preserving condition: D_N is a genuine circuit for the same H_N inputs, R_N is explicitly row-indexed without advice, and each residual row has correction cost O(N).

equations.label: residual_patch_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when each residual row can be patched by a direct equality-and-table circuit in the named row model.

equations.label: subthreshold_residual_collapse
equations.valid_when: Valid when gamma is a fixed positive slack and lower-order encoding costs are absorbed into o(1).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A sparse residual R_N with small D_N is a falsifier for any claimed N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: No-go test for functionalized certificates and local consistency proofs that leave only sparse semantic disagreement.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Sparse-row residual compression lemma: if a certificate-mediated approximant D_N agrees with H_N^SAT outside a residual row set R_N, then subthreshold residual size collapses the intended N^{1+epsilon} lower bound.

dependency_updates.description: Every proposed MCSP/MKtP or DirectClusterSound carrier must now report alpha_ad and compare it with theta before any extraction claim is valid.
The known transfer delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) remains usable only after the adaptive-cover, residual, and advice ledgers are passed.
Hard-row or hard-certificate selection must be E-searchable without advice; nonuniform selection is a route-level contradiction carrier.
Functional certificate substitutions must satisfy a>max{rho,q} and avoid sparse-row residual compression before they can support the main theorem-shaped packet.

falsifiers: falsifier: an accepted MCSP/MKtP certificate whose Merkle, checkpoint, or cluster openings give alpha_ad<theta immediately yields a small unrestricted circuit for the row.
falsifier: a hard-row selector that chooses pi or a row index using nonuniform advice fails to define an E-uniform target language.

falsifier: DirectClusterSound acceptance based only on local consistency and ordinary soundness may functionalize SAT labels into a sparse residual D_N plus R_N, collapsing the claimed N^{1+epsilon} lower bound.
falsifier: beta-zero XOR parameters with a<=max{rho,q} cannot transfer a source lower bound to SAT circuit lower bounds by substitution.
falsifier: low-complexity sparse or parity rows accepted by the certificate model show that the certificate is not circuit-sensitive enough for MCSP no-side soundness.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: With polynomial summaries and openers, alpha_cluster=1-lambda+o(1). If lambda>1-theta, every accepted row is subthreshold-easy, so the certificate is invalid; if lambda<=1-theta, the carrier avoids this falsifier but pays large summary volume and still must prove genuine row hardness without advice.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 74 instantiates the adaptive-cover obstruction on a concrete DirectClusterSound-style carrier. The contribution-making move is a finite falsifier: low-cover MCSP/MKtP certificates do not merely look weak; they give explicit unrestricted row circuits below the claimed threshold. The positive source theorem is still open and essentially requires high adaptive cover dimension plus advice-free hard-row generation.
